cases.summary: Apartment: plumbing shifted to the tenant (multi-unit, so void) and both deposit deadlines too long.
Single-family house: allowed repair shift, holdover lockout, deposit with no disclosure.
Texted garage-apartment rental: power shutoff for late rent, 7-day landlord termination notice.
Condo tower: 2-hour any-time entry, broad exculpation with a savings phrase.
Apartment: code-complaint gag, removal for late rent, short move-out notice; compliant abandoned-property clause with legend.
Retail shopping-center lease: not residential, so no findings.
Lease pasted from a forwarded email with quote markers: commingled deposit, calendar-day notice, storm clause.
Duplex with surety bond: allowed plumbing shift, punitive-damages fee carve-out, ban on all national flags.
Short compliant apartment lease with a $0 deposit.

findings.title: Deposit return deadline
findings.problem: The lease gives the landlord 45 days to return the deposit when there is no claim. Florida requires 15 days or less, so this term is void.

span.quote: If Landlord makes no claim, the deposit will be returned within 45 days after the lease ends.

findings.suggestedFix: Landlord will return the deposit when there is no claim within 15 days after the termination of the rental agreement.

findings.title: Deposit claim notice deadline
findings.problem: The lease gives the landlord 60 days to send written notice of a claim on the deposit. Florida requires 30 days or less, so this term is void.

span.quote: If Landlord intends to make a claim, Landlord will send written notice within 60 days after the lease ends.

findings.suggestedFix: Landlord will send written notice of a claim on the deposit within 30 days after the termination of the rental agreement.

findings.title: Waiver of landlord's maintenance duties
findings.problem: The lease shifts the landlord's code, structural or plumbing duties to the tenant. For a unit that is not a single-family home or duplex, these duties can't be waived.

span.quote: Tenant is responsible for all plumbing repairs inside the Premises, including pipes, drains, water lines, and fixtures, regardless of cause, and shall hire a licensed plumber at Tenant's expense.

findings.suggestedFix: Landlord will comply with applicable building, housing, and health codes and keep the structural components and plumbing in good repair as required by s. 83.51(1), Florida Statutes.

findings.problem: The lease takes a deposit but doesn't include the required deposit disclosure. This can also be given in a separate written notice within 30 days, and doesn't apply to landlords with fewer than five units.

findings.title: Lockout
findings.problem: The lease allows the landlord to change the locks or otherwise keep the tenant out. Florida prohibits self-help lockouts; only a court eviction can remove a tenant.

span.quote: If Tenants remain in the Residence after the lease ends without Landlord's written consent, Landlord may change the locks and remove the Tenants from the Residence.

findings.suggestedFix: Delete the clause. Landlord may recover possession only through a court eviction.

findings.title: Notice to end a periodic tenancy
findings.problem: For a month-to-month tenancy the lease allows the landlord to give 7 days' notice. Florida requires at least 30 days before the end of the period.

span.quote: i can end it with 7 days' notice. you need to give me 30 days' notice.

findings.suggestedFix: Either party may end this month-to-month tenancy by giving written notice at least 30 days before the end of a rental period.

findings.title: Utility shutoff

findings.title: Notice before entry for repairs
findings.problem: The lease lets the landlord enter for repairs with 2 hours' notice. Florida requires at least 24 hours' notice for repairs (emergencies excepted).

span.quote: Owner or Owner's contractors may enter the Unit at any time to make repairs after giving Renter at least 2 hours' notice by text message.

findings.suggestedFix: Except in an emergency, Landlord will give Tenant at least 24 hours' notice before entering to make repairs.

findings.title: Hours for entry to make repairs
findings.problem: The lease lets the landlord enter for repairs outside 7:30 a.m.–8:00 p.m. Florida limits repair entry to those hours (entry to protect or preserve the premises is separate).

span.quote: Owner or Owner's contractors may enter the Unit at any time to make repairs after giving Renter at least 2 hours' notice by text message.

findings.suggestedFix: Landlord may enter to make repairs between 7:30 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. with at least 24 hours' notice, and at any time to protect or preserve the premises.

findings.title: Limit on landlord liability
findings.problem: The lease tries to release the landlord from liability the law imposes. Florida makes this kind of clause void.

span.quote: Owner will not be liable for any injury, loss, or damage to Renter or Renter's property occurring in the Unit or the building, from any cause, unless otherwise required by law.

findings.suggestedFix: Delete the clause. Each party remains responsible for its own obligations and liability under law.

findings.problem: The lease requires 15 days' notice from the tenant before the term ends. Florida allows only 30 to 60 days.

span.quote: Tenant must notify Landlord in writing at least 15 days before the end of the term if Tenant will not renew.

findings.suggestedFix: Either party must give written notice at least 30 days (and no more than 60 days) before the end of the lease term if they do not intend to renew.

findings.title: Retaliation against the tenant
findings.problem: The lease penalizes the tenant (higher rent, fewer services or termination) for protected conduct such as complaining to a code agency. Florida prohibits retaliation.

span.quote: Any such contact before then is a default under this lease, and Landlord may terminate the lease.

findings.suggestedFix: Delete the clause.

findings.title: Removing the tenant's belongings
findings.problem: The lease lets the landlord remove the tenant's belongings without a surrender, abandonment or court eviction. Florida prohibits this.

span.quote: If rent is more than 15 days late, Landlord may remove Tenant's belongings from the Unit and hold them until Tenant pays all rent due.

findings.suggestedFix: Landlord may remove Tenant's personal property only after surrender, abandonment, or a lawful eviction.

findings.title: Notice for unpaid rent
findings.problem: The lease counts weekends or holidays in the unpaid-rent notice period. Florida excludes Saturdays, Sundays and court-observed holidays.

findings.title: Waiver of attorney fees

span.quote: The prevailing party in any action may recover reasonable attorney fees, except that no attorney fees shall be awarded in any action in which punitive or exemplary damages are sought.

findings.suggestedFix: In any action to enforce this lease or Part II of Chapter 83, the prevailing party may recover reasonable attorney fees and court costs.
